A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RA-RAG work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-M are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original multi-source question-answering experiments, ablations, efficiency measurements, and real-world source reliability estimates in Sections 5-6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, component analyses, computational measurements, and evaluations of three real-world sources.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same reliability estimation, filtering, semantic clustering, weighted voting, and source selection procedures. The new concluding example sketches prospective use for long-form generation without revising the specified RA-RAG algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NQ, TriviaQA, single-hop HotpotQA queries, and claims from two politicians and one X account. The long-form and multi-hop applications discussed in v4 are not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Oracle WMV, MV, Vanilla RAG, Robust RAG, Self-RAG, and Vanilla LLM retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons, including Self-RAG in Appendix E. Perplexity is added as motivational context, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The source priors, model configurations, 200/1,400 estimation/test split, top-3 versus top-10 retrieval settings, κ=4, and accuracy metric are unchanged. The separate filtering-ablation settings and real-world sampling and evaluation procedures are also retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same filtering and threshold ablations, source-selection analyses, adversarial tests, computational-efficiency comparisons, and qualitative examples. Sections 5.3 and Appendices C, F, G, K, and M introduce no new analyses in v4.

E5.justification: Both versions state that benchmark results are averaged over 10 random trials and retain the same correlation statistics and p-value reporting for real-world reliability estimation. No repeated-run or uncertainty reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged, including Tables 1-3 and A1-A15. For example, Table 3 retains estimated reliabilities of 0.175, 0.539, and 0.660. Relocated appendix captions do not change result attribution.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, filtering definition, weighted-voting equations, and reliability update are unchanged. v4 numbers the previously unnumbered filtering equation and renumbers subsequent equations; it adds no formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The main robustness, scalability, and reliability-estimation claims remain. The conclusion newly states that RA-RAG extends to long-form and multi-hop question answering, modestly broadening claimed applicability beyond the evaluated short-form setting.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains that source granularity depends on the application, ranging from individual accounts to news websites. The conclusion adds a decomposition-and-synthesis example and identifies heterogeneous-source datasets for complex tasks as future work. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds an explicit code-and-data availability statement with a RA-RAG repository link in the abstract, absent from v3. Existing implementation details, prompts, preprocessing descriptions, thresholds, and hardware information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Perplexity AI (2025) and Shrivastava (2024) to motivate commercial RAG misinformation risks. Section 4.2 changes its description from utilizing to extending Li and Yu's WMV method. The broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized additions to the abstract, introduction, source explanation, and conclusion, adds acknowledgments, and removes the Limitations section number. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content. Captions for Tables A7-A15 move from above to below the tables, some main-text floats shift within the layout, and printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: The new code/data pointer and clearer explanation of source granularity modestly improve documented accessibility and conceptual clarity. The broader applicability discussion remains unevaluated, so it does not strengthen the empirical evidence. With methods and results preserved, the net gain is limited to documentation and exposition.
